extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders in FCC rulemaking (ISPs, consumers, telecom lawyers, public commenters, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards relevant to preparing or evaluating comments and regulatory actions in FCC rulemaking addressing the open Internet / broadband internet access service (BIAS), including transparency, conduct rules, Title II classification, outage reporting, and related PRA information collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit blocking, throttling, paid or affiliated prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Report and Order reinstates straightforward, clear rules that prohibit blocking, throttling, or engaging in paid or affiliated prioritization arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit conduct prohibition adopted to safeguard the open internet, protect free expression, encourage competition and innovation, and protect consumers and public safety. Comments and compliance assessments should address whether specific practices constitute blocking, throttling, or paid/affiliated prioritization under the rule language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency Rule disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person providing broadband internet access service shall publicly disclose accurate information regarding the network management practices, performance characteristics, and commercial terms of its broadband internet access services sufficient to enable consumers to make informed choices regarding the purchase and use of such services and entrepreneurs and other small businesses to develop, market, and maintain internet offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must be made via a publicly available, easily accessible mechanism. The transparency rule is subject to PRA information-collection requirements; commenters should address clarity, practicality, and burden (see PRA-related criteria). The rule may be enhanced in the Report and Order; submissions can propose specifics about content, format, frequency, and accessibility of disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: General conduct standard: unreasonable interference or unreasonable disadvantage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Report and Order reinstates a general conduct standard that prohibits unreasonable interference or unreasonable disadvantage to consumers or edge providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard operates alongside specific prohibitions (e.g., blocking/throttling) and requires evaluative judgments about 'reasonable' vs 'unreasonable' conduct. Comments should supply concrete examples, metrics, or tests to determine when conduct crosses the threshold into 'unreasonable' interference or disadvantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassification of BIAS as a Title II telecommunications service
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes/classifies broadband internet access service as a telecommunications service under Title II of the Communications Act to provide the Commission with authority necessary to safeguard the open internet, advance national security, protect public safety, and protect consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reclassification is framed as enabling stronger federal authority (including preemption) while allowing the Commission to tailor application of Title II. Arguments for or against reclassification should address statutory interpretation, impacts on deployment and competition, national security and public-safety implications, and legal defensibility (including preemption considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored forbearance of Title II application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order establishes broad, tailored forbearance of the Commission's application of Title II to broadband providers while maintaining Title II provisions the Commission needs to fulfill its obligations and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a balancing mechanism intended to preserve needed regulatory tools while minimizing burdens. Comments or assessments should identify which Title II provisions should be retained or forborne from and provide justification tied to benefits, burdens, and statutory goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption of inconsistent state open-internet laws / national uniform approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Reclassification will put the Commission's authority to preempt any inconsistent state laws on substantially stronger legal footing, enabling the Commission to create a uniform set of open internet standards and avoid state-by-state requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should consider the potential burden on ISPs (especially small ISPs), the adequacy of federal standards to protect consumers nationwide, and the legal basis for preemption. Commenters may discuss whether federal uniformity or state variation better serves competition and consumer protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outage reporting to NORS and DIRS (BIAS providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requiring mobile and fixed broadband internet access service providers to submit reports of outages to the FCC's Network Outage Reporting System (NORS) and Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal is intended to improve resilience and cybersecurity situational awareness. Commenters should address what outages must be reported, reporting thresholds and timelines, data fields required, confidentiality concerns, and the administrative burden of reporting. The rule may also propose 'after action' reports at the Commission's direction for providers that report in DIRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require providers to supply location of mobile recovery assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes requiring current and future service providers to supply the Commission with information concerning the location of their mobile recovery assets, including the location of Cells on Wheels (COWs) and Cells on Light Trucks (COLTs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement supports emergency preparedness and recovery. Comments should address data accuracy, frequency of updates, national-security or confidentiality concerns, and any privacy or commercial-sensitivity protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Georouting requirements for 988 calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes to require implementation of one or more georouting solutions for wireless calls to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline to ensure that calls are routed based on the geographic location for the origin of the call, rather than the area code and exchange associated with a wireless phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should evaluate technological feasibility, accuracy, privacy implications, implementation costs, and timelines. Proposals may compare alternative georouting methods and present data on expected improvements in routing accuracy and public-safety outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA information-collection comment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission requests public comment under the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA), commenters should address: whether the proposed collection is necessary for the proper performance of the Commission's functions (practical utility); the accuracy of the Commission's burden estimate; ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; ways to minimize respondent burden, including use of automated techniques; and ways to reduce the burden on small business concerns with fewer than 25 employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are required elements for PRA review and OMB approval; substantive comments should provide alternative burden estimates, propose streamlined data elements, suggest standardized formats, and show how the collection would be used by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation and disclosure requirements regarding foreign adversary control
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed adoption of new attestation and disclosure requirements for holders of Commission-granted licenses, leases, authorizations, permits, grants and other approvals to enhance public transparency over Foreign Adversary Control over U.S. communications network operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should consider scope (which holders and approvals), the form and frequency of attestation, verification mechanisms, enforcement, confidentiality protections, and trade/foreign-investment implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming CFR rule parts to reflect court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conform certain rule parts in the Code of Federal Regulations to reflect the rules that are actually in effect as a result of court decisions (e.g., Ohio Telecom and Iowa Utilities Board II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural standard to ensure regulatory text matches judicially-effective rules. Comments or redline suggestions should identify inconsistencies, cite controlling decisions, and propose precise regulatory text changes.
